description: Pod health, message flow, journal, HTTP API, storage and memory for a Graylog Helm release.

spec.description: Messages accepted by inputs, per Graylog node.
spec.title: Message input rate (msg/s)

spec.description: How full the on-disk message journal is, as Graylog reports it. Compare with the journal PVC fill in the Storage section.
spec.title: Journal utilization (%)

spec.description: Messages written out to the indexer, per Graylog node.
spec.title: Message output rate (msg/s)

spec.description: Input positive, output negative on a shared axis. Symmetry means Graylog is keeping up; a widening gap means the journal is filling.
spec.title: Message rate in / out

spec.description: Absolute journal bytes against message_journal_max_size. Note this limit, not the PVC, is what gl_journal_utilization is a percentage of - the volume can be larger.
spec.title: Journal size vs limit

spec.description: Chart-owned pods where every container reports ready.
spec.title: Healthy pods

spec.description: Append positive, read negative. Sustained append above read is what fills the journal.
spec.title: Journal append vs read rate

spec.description: The metric graylog.lifecycle.preStopDrain waits on: the drain hook polls this via the exporter on localhost and holds shutdown until it reaches zero.
spec.title: Uncommitted journal entries

spec.description: Segment count. Growth alongside size means old segments are not being reclaimed.
spec.title: Journal segments

spec.description: Where per-message time goes inside Graylog: decode, parse, then pipeline rules.
spec.title: Message processing latency (p95)

spec.description: Per-filter-type cost - extractors and similar. A slow type here shows up as process buffer pressure.
spec.title: Filter execution time (p95) by type

spec.description: Messages that failed to index. Anything sustained above zero means data is being dropped or parked.
spec.title: Indexing failures

spec.description: A falling hit rate means rule lookups are recompiling more often.
spec.title: Pipeline interpreter cache hit rate

spec.description: Per-stream ingest rate. Streams are labelled by id; 000000000000000000000001 is All messages.
spec.title: Stream throughput (msg/s)

spec.expr: count((max by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{job="$ksm_job", namespace="$namespace", container=~"graylog-app|graylog-datanode|geoip-updater|mongod|mongodb-agent", reason=~"CrashLoopBackOff|ImagePullBackOff|ErrImagePull|CreateContainerConfigError|CreateContainerError|InvalidImageName|RunContainerError"}) > 0) or (max by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_terminated_reason{job="$ksm_job", namespace="$namespace", container=~"graylog-app|graylog-datanode|geoip-updater|mongod|mongodb-agent", reason=~"OOMKilled|Error"}) > 0)) or vector(0)

spec.description: Pods in a real error state: CrashLoopBackOff, image pull failures, CreateContainerConfigError, OOMKilled. Pods still starting are counted under Starting, not here.
spec.title: Failed

spec.description: Each license condition as reported by Graylog. Non-zero means the condition is active.
spec.title: License status

spec.description: Bytes ingested over a trailing 24h window.
spec.title: Daily input traffic

spec.description: Bytes written out over a trailing 24h window.
spec.title: Daily output traffic

spec.description: Shorter window than the daily view, so short spikes stay visible.
spec.title: 15-minute input traffic rate

spec.description: Journal fill over time. Sustained growth is the early warning that output is falling behind input.
spec.title: Journal utilization over time

spec.description: Requests per second served by the Graylog REST API, from the request-duration summary's count.
spec.title: API request rate

spec.description: Request duration quantiles reported by Graylog. p0.999 is excluded: long-poll endpoints dominate it and flatten the axis.
spec.title: API request latency

spec.expr: count((min by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_ready{job="$ksm_job", namespace="$namespace", container=~"graylog-app|graylog-datanode|geoip-updater|mongod|mongodb-agent"}) == 0) unless ((max by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{job="$ksm_job", namespace="$namespace", container=~"graylog-app|graylog-datanode|geoip-updater|mongod|mongodb-agent", reason=~"CrashLoopBackOff|ImagePullBackOff|ErrImagePull|CreateContainerConfigError|CreateContainerError|InvalidImageName|RunContainerError"}) > 0) or (max by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_terminated_reason{job="$ksm_job", namespace="$namespace", container=~"graylog-app|graylog-datanode|geoip-updater|mongod|mongodb-agent", reason=~"OOMKilled|Error"}) > 0))) or vector(0)

spec.description: Chart pods not ready yet but not failing: Pending, PodInitializing, or a rollout in progress.
spec.title: Starting

spec.description: gRPC calls per second per method across the forwarder's control and message channels.
spec.title: Forwarder call rate by method

spec.description: Per-method p95. ControlService calls are config polls; message-channel latency is the ingest path.
spec.title: Forwarder call latency (p95) by method

spec.description: Total provisioned capacity across all mounted Data Node volumes. Orphaned volumes are not counted - nothing mounts them.
spec.title: Data Node capacity

spec.description: Cluster-wide fill. Colours follow the OpenSearch watermarks: amber at 85%, orange at 90%, red at the 95% flood stage.
spec.title: Used % of capacity

spec.description: Bytes OpenSearch can still write before hitting the 95% flood stage, at which point every index on an affected node goes read-only and ingest to it stops.
spec.title: Writable before flood stage

spec.description: Bytes before the 85% low watermark, where OpenSearch stops allocating new shards to a node. This is the first threshold that changes behaviour, so it is the one to plan against.
spec.title: Headroom to low watermark

spec.description: Per-volume fill against the OpenSearch watermarks, drawn as dashed lines at 85, 90 and 95%.
spec.title: Data Node disk used % with watermarks

spec.description: Remaining writable bytes per Data Node volume before its flood stage. A volume at zero here has its indices forced read-only.
spec.title: Writable space per volume (to flood stage)

spec.description: OpenSearch cluster status as Graylog reports it. Yellow means replicas unassigned; red means a primary shard is missing and those indices cannot be written.
spec.title: Indexer cluster health

spec.description: Time until each volume reaches 95%, from its 6h growth rate. Volumes that are flat or shrinking are omitted rather than shown as infinite. Treat this as a trend, not a forecast: a retention change or a traffic spike moves it sharply.
spec.title: Projected time to flood stage

spec.description: Each Data Node volume as a percentage of its capacity, labelled by node group. Amber at 75%, red at 85%.
spec.title: Data Node PVC used %

spec.description: The Graylog server's journal volume. This is the disk behind gl_journal_utilization - if the journal fills, ingest stops.
spec.title: Graylog journal PVC used %

spec.description: Growth trend per Data Node volume. A single volume diverging from its group usually means uneven shard allocation.
spec.title: Data Node PVC used % over time

spec.description: Journal volume growth. Compare with 'Journal utilization over time' - Graylog's own figure is capped by message_journal_max_size, which may be smaller than the volume.
spec.title: Graylog journal PVC used % over time

spec.description: Absolute bytes for every Data Node and Graylog journal volume. Capacity is dotted.
spec.title: PVC used vs capacity (bytes)

spec.description: Every Data Node and Graylog journal PVC, orphans first. An orphaned PVC is bound but no pod mounts it - usually a node group scaled down without removing its volumes. It still costs money. Size columns are blank for orphans because the kubelet only measures mounted volumes.
spec.title: PVC details

spec.description: CPU cores. Node group is derived from the pod name (<release>-datanode-<group>-<ordinal>); the primary group shows as 'default'. This is the node GROUP name, not the OpenSearch role - group names are user-chosen and need not match the roles they carry. Requests and limits pin job=kube-state-metrics because opencost also exports requests, which would double-count.
spec.title: Data Node CPU: usage vs requests vs limits
